hints.title: Quadratic Pair Search Obstacle
hints.text: Evaluating every pair of lines requires quadratic comparisons. If you start with the widest possible container at both ends, which boundary should move inward to have any hope of finding a larger area?

hints.title: Shorter Line Limits Volume
hints.text: Container area is limited by the shorter line. Moving the taller line inward can only decrease the width without any chance to increase the limiting height, so the shorter line must always move inward.

hints.title: Two Pointers Inward Scan
hints.text: Initialize left at 0 and right at n - 1 with max_area = 0. In each step, calculate the area using (right - left) * min(height[left], height[right]) and update max_area. Then advance whichever pointer has the smaller height inward until the pointers meet.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of height array (2 <= N <= 10^5)
complexity.notes: Single pass where pointers start at opposite ends and advance toward each other.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Checking all pairs of lines takes O(N^2) time. For N = 10^5, N * (N - 1) / 2 = ~5 * 10^9 operations, exceeding the 1-second limit.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Greedy inward two-pointer traversal requires O(1) auxiliary space and eliminates suboptimal configurations without evaluating them.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Formal justification for moving the shorter pointer (proving no larger container can be formed with the discarded line), O(1) extra space, and clean code.

solutions.approach: Inward Two Pointers Moving Shorter Bar
